title.en: The secret ballot, and forming a government
title.fr: Le scrutin secret et la formation du gouvernement

text.en: The law in Canada protects your right to a secret ballot. Nobody may watch you while you vote, and nobody should look at the choice you made.
text.fr: Au Canada, la loi protège votre droit au scrutin secret. Personne ne peut vous regarder voter, et personne ne devrait regarder le choix que vous avez fait.

source.quote: Canadian law secures the right to a secret ballot. This means that no one can watch you vote and no one should look at how you voted.

text.en: You are free to talk about your vote if you want to. But no one has the right to make you say how you voted: not your family, not your employer and not your union representative.
text.fr: Vous êtes libre de parler de votre vote si vous le voulez. Mais personne n'a le droit de vous obliger à dire comment vous avez voté : ni votre famille, ni votre employeur, ni votre représentant syndical.

source.quote: You may choose to discuss how you voted with others, but no one, including family members, your employer or union representative, has the right to insist that you tell them how you voted.

text.en: As soon as the polling stations close, election officers count the ballots. Then the results are shared on the radio, on TV and in newspapers.
text.fr: Dès que les bureaux de scrutin ferment, les membres du personnel électoral comptent les bulletins. Les résultats sont ensuite annoncés à la radio, à la télévision et dans les journaux.

source.quote: Immediately after the polling stations close, election officers count the ballots and the results are announced on radio and television, and in the newspapers.

text.en: Usually, after an election, the Governor General asks the leader of the party that won the largest number of House of Commons seats to form the government.
text.fr: D'habitude, après une élection, le gouverneur général demande au chef du parti qui a remporté le plus grand nombre de sièges à la Chambre des communes de former le gouvernement.

source.quote: Ordinarily, after an election, the leader of the political party with the most seats in the House of Commons is invited by the Governor General to form the government.

text.en: The Governor General then appoints that party leader, who becomes the Prime Minister.
text.fr: Le gouverneur général nomme ensuite ce chef de parti, qui devient premier ministre.

source.quote: After being appointed by the Governor General, the leader of this party becomes the Prime Minister.

text.en: When the governing party holds half the House of Commons seats or more, it is a majority government.
text.fr: Quand le parti au pouvoir détient la moitié des sièges ou plus à la Chambre des communes, on parle d'un gouvernement majoritaire.

source.quote: If the party in power holds at least half of the seats in the House of Commons, this is called a majority government.

text.en: When the governing party holds under half the House of Commons seats, it is a minority government.
text.fr: Quand le parti au pouvoir détient moins de la moitié des sièges à la Chambre des communes, on parle d'un gouvernement minoritaire.

source.quote: If the party in power holds less than half of the seats in the House of Commons, this is called a minority government.

text.en: The Prime Minister and the governing party stay in charge only while most MPs support them, or have confidence in them.
text.fr: Le premier ministre et le parti au pouvoir restent à la tête du gouvernement seulement tant que la majorité des députés les appuient, c'est-à-dire leur font confiance.

source.quote: The Prime Minister and the party in power run the government as long as they have the support or confidence of the majority of the MPs.

text.en: If most MPs vote against an important government decision, the governing party is defeated. Usually the Prime Minister then asks the Governor General, acting for the Sovereign, to call an election.
text.fr: Si la majorité des députés de la Chambre des communes votent contre une décision importante du gouvernement, le parti au pouvoir est défait. D'habitude, le premier ministre demande alors au gouverneur général, au nom du souverain, de déclencher une élection.

source.quote: If a majority of the members of the House of Commons vote against a major government decision, the party in power is defeated, which usually results in the Prime Minister asking the Governor General, on behalf of the Sovereign, to call an election.
